Britain has invaded or fought on the soil of roughly 171 of the world's 193 countries. The black patches on this map are the ones it never got round to — and they are a stranger list than the red.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ The count comes from Stuart Laycock, who in 2012 worked through the military history of every UN member state one at a time. He wasn't a professional historian; he started after his young son asked him the question.

2/ The never-invaded list: Sweden, Belarus, Andorra, Luxembourg, Monaco, the Vatican, Mongolia, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, Bolivia, Paraguay, Guatemala, Mali, Chad, Ivory Coast, Burundi and a few small island states.

3/ “Invaded” is doing heavy lifting. Laycock counts outright colonial conquest alongside privateer raids, brief troop landings and British forces fighting a wider war on someone else's soil. It's a generous definition, and he says so.

4/ Sweden is the best anomaly. It spent 1810 to 1812 formally at war with Britain, under Napoleonic pressure to join the Continental System — and the two never actually fought. No battles, no landings, a war that existed on paper.

5/ The landlocked clusters in Central Asia and the Sahel show the real pattern. British reach followed water: navy first, army after. Places far from a coast and off the trade routes were largely places Britain never bothered with.

6/ Whether 171 is the right number is arguable — tighten the definition and it falls. The shape of the map is not arguable. A maritime empire left almost no coastline on Earth untouched.

Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
